subject: chemistry
content:
Amongst the following the total number of compounds whose aqueous solution turns red litmus paper blue is
KCN, K2SO4, (NH4)2C2O4, NaCl, Zn(NO3)2, FeCl3, K2CO3, NH4NO3 and LiCN
explanation:
Aqueous solutions turn red litmus paper blue if they are basic (pH > 7). Basic solutions are formed by the hydrolysis of salts containing the anion of a weak acid and cation of a strong base:

  • KCN: Salt of strong base (KOH) and weak acid (HCN) → Basic (Turns red litmus blue)
  • K2SO4: Salt of strong base (KOH) and strong acid (H2SO4) → Neutral
  • (NH4)2C2O4: Salt of weak base (NH4OH) and weak acid (H2C2O4) → Nearly neutral / weakly acidic
  • NaCl: Salt of strong base (NaOH) and strong acid (HCl) → Neutral
  • Zn(NO3)2: Salt of weak base (Zn(OH)2) and strong acid (HNO3) → Acidic
  • FeCl3: Salt of weak base (Fe(OH)3) and strong acid (HCl) → Acidic
  • K2CO3: Salt of strong base (KOH) and weak acid (H2CO3) → Basic (Turns red litmus blue)
  • NH4NO3: Salt of weak base (NH4OH) and strong acid (HNO3) → Acidic
  • LiCN: Salt of strong base (LiOH) and weak acid (HCN) → Basic (Turns red litmus blue)

Hence, the basic compounds are KCN, K2CO3, and LiCN. The total number is 3.
